chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man hunted game while he was in the state of Ihram; should I eat from it while I am in the state of Halal? He said: 'I would do it.' I said to him: What about a man who acquires unlawful wealth? He said: 'This is not like that; may Allah have mercy on you, for that is upon him (the owner).'

key_terms.حَلاَلٌ: One not in the state of Ihram (free from Ihram restrictions)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can I eat game hunted by someone else who was in Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the personal prohibition of consuming hunted game while in Ihram and the general permissibility of consuming it once the hunter is free, emphasizing that the restriction is on the act of hunting itself. He further clarifies that unlike the specific ritual impurity of Ihram violations, unlawfully acquired wealth remains the property of the owner, meaning its consumption or use by others does not carry the same ritual penalty, highlighting the distinction between *haram* (forbidden) and *ghasb* (usurped) in Shia jurisprudence.
